h2: Water Heater Repair & Installation Bali – Hot Water, Sorted
intro: No hot water in your villa? Whether it's an electric tank in Seminyak, a gas unit in Uluwatu or a rooftop solar setup in Canggu, I diagnose the fault and fix it properly. This page covers what typically goes wrong with heaters across Bali, what a repair or new installation involves, and exactly what to send on WhatsApp so we sort it in one visit.

sections.h3: Why Villa Heaters Fail in Bali's Climate
sections.text: Most units in Canggu, Ubud or Uluwatu die for one of three reasons: a burnt-out heating element, a drifted thermostat, or a corroded anode rod that has let rust eat into the tank. Tropical humidity accelerates limescale buildup, especially where borehole water is hard — common around Seminyak and Jimbaran. Rooftop solar collectors often just stop delivering warm output after a stretch of cloudy days without any visible damage; the panel and circulation pump both need checking before you assume the system is dead.

sections.h3: What a Repair or New Install Actually Involves
sections.text: Depending on whether you run an electric tank, gas burner or rooftop solar, I trace the fault first, then replace whatever part has gone: elements, thermostats, anodes, gaskets or pressure-relief valves. For new installations across Denpasar, Sanur, Kuta & Legian, Nusa Dua or Kerobokan & Umalas, the job means sizing the heater to your household, routing pipework, connecting safely to the electrical panel, and pressure-testing every joint. You receive a clear quote from photos sent over WhatsApp before any work begins.

sections.h3: Three Things to Send Before I Head Out
sections.text: Grab me these on WhatsApp so I arrive with the right parts: a short video showing the actual problem (breaker tripping, water weeping from the tank base, or simply lukewarm output), a photo of the unit's nameplate displaying wattage or gas rating, and where it sits — bathroom wall, utility room or rooftop. If the breaker trips, note which circuit number it is. That context saves a second visit and means one trip fixes it rather than two.

sections.h3: Keeping Your Heater Alive Between Visits
sections.text: A quick annual flush knocks out limescale, swapping the anode rod when it's more than half consumed stops internal corrosion, and confirming the pressure-relief valve still clicks when you lift its tab prevents silent tank failure. On solar rooftops in Uluwatu or Canggu, clear leaf debris from the collector panel and verify the circulation pump kicks in at dawn. Ten minutes of maintenance now spares you standing under cold water in Ubud because the element quietly died over the weekend.

faq.q: How do I know if my heater needs a repair or a full replacement?
faq.a: Send photos and a short clip of the issue on WhatsApp — most faults in Bali villas come down to a single part like an element or thermostat that costs far less to swap than replacing the whole unit.

faq.q: Do you handle electric, gas and solar heaters all across Bali?
faq.a: Yes, I work on all three types across Canggu, Ubud, Seminyak, Uluwatu, Sanur, Jimbaran, Kuta & Legian, Nusa Dua, Denpasar and Kerobokan & Umalas.

faq.q: What should I send before booking so we fix it in one visit?
faq.a: A brief video showing the problem, a photo of the nameplate, and the unit's location — that way I bring the correct parts and we sort it without a second trip.
